verdict.rationale: ReadMe documents four theme presets with brand colors and typography in Appearance settings, custom CSS (variables or rules) and JavaScript/include tags, and fully custom MDX components, which covers most of the branding story. Custom CSS/JS is plan-gated, layout control beyond presets is not explicitly documented, and independent corroboration is limited to one community note on color settings. Missing for 10: explicit layout/navigation customization docs, clarity on which plans unlock custom CSS/JS, and independent hands-on corroboration of deep custom CSS/JS/component branding.

support.subject: As a DevRel lead, I customize themes, fonts, and layout — down to custom CSS/JS or my own components — so the docs match my brand

citations.quote: Set your hub's look from four theme presets, then tune brand colors and typography in Appearance settings.
Apply your own CSS, JavaScript, and include tags to your hub, with the plan requirements and toggles for each.
Customize your docs with CSS using either CSS variables or custom CSS rules. The most flexible is to use CSS variables.
build fully custom MDX components beyond GitBook's block editor
Write MDX in ReadMe, including the JSX syntax and the places where it behaves differently from plain Markdown.
